I’m considering how to produce three copies of a 10-row grid through a reflected pattern. This involves reversing the input sequence, then following it forward and reversing again to get a structure like [r9...r0][r0...r9][r9...r0]. The output should mirror tile the base grid both vertically and horizontally. I plan to use a test grid of 8x4 to generate a larger output of 24x8. def transform(grid):
    """Mirror-tile the grid three times vertically and twice horizontally."""
    if not grid or any(not row for row in grid):
        return []
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    if any(len(row) != w for row in grid):
        raise ValueError("ragged grid")
    vertical_rows = list(reversed(grid)) + [row[:] for row in grid] + list(reversed(grid))
    return [list(reversed(row)) + row[:] for row in vertical_rows]
PY
